newsitem.title: USA: ANALYSIS-Tame US inflation softens big Q4 GDP rise.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSIS-Tame US inflation softens big Q4 GDP rise.

text.p: Soft inflationary numbers proved to be the silver lining in the black cloud of a whopping increase in fourth quarter gross domestic product.

Far from falling off the track, the bond market remained steady after the U.S. Commerce Department said on Friday that fourth quarter GDP rose 4.7 percent. The GDP price index, however, rose only 1.8 percent and the implicit price deflator rose 1.4 percent.
"The bond market had been warned this number could come strong and had priced that in. But the inflationary number was surprisingly good," said Suzanne Rizzo, economist at MFR Inc.
In addition, economists said the big boost in trade seen in the fourth quarter should be more than offset by declines in the first quarter due to the surging dollar.
"Any time you have a growth rate of 4.7 percent it's strong. Anything over 3.0 percent is strong," said Hugh Johnson, chief economist at First Albany Corp.
Nonetheless, investors seem convinced the story going forward remains the same: steady growth with soft inflation and the expectation that the figures would moderate in the first half of this year.
Johnson said commercial construction came in strong with a 4.2 percent rise and that was unlikely to be sustainable moving into 1997.
Exports, rising 25.5 percent, also would fall not only due to the dollar's strength, but because a good part of the figure may reflect rising energy costs, Johnson said.
"If you take apart that figure I'm sure there's got to be an energy price component due to the cold weather and rising price of heating oil," Johnson said.
Business inventories also held steady, implying neither a slowdown nor a pickup in production.
"The markets, of course, are looking ahead and they're seeing growth coming down to the 2.5 percent to 3.0 percent range (in the first quarter)," Johnson said.
